articles.title: Canada Holds Student Arrivals Target at Up to 150,000 a Year Through 2029
articles.excerpt: IRCC's 2027–2029 Immigration Levels Plan extends the student target into 2029 and holds total new temporary resident arrivals at 370,000 a year — while actual student arrivals run at about half the target.
articles.image_caption: The flag of Canada. Canada's 2027–2029 Immigration Levels Plan holds new international student arrivals at up to 150,000 a year through 2029.

sources.label: IRCC — Supplementary Information for the 2027–2029 Immigration Levels Plan

articles.nri_angle: Indian students are Canada's largest international cohort (94,025 permits effective in 2025); the extended 150,000-a-year arrivals target sets their planning horizon through 2029.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Pune's Swasti Patil Wins India's First Gold at European Girls' Informatics Olympiad
articles.excerpt: Listed as 'Unschooled, Pune' in India's official olympiad records, Swasti Vitthal Patil scored 581 points in Cesenatico, Italy, a year after winning bronze in Germany — leading India's best-ever EGOI team result.

sources.label: The Hindu BusinessLine (Sasken / PR Newswire release)

articles.nri_angle: An unschooled Pune student's route through India's open olympiad pathway to an international gold is a reference point for diaspora families weighing alternative schooling.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: 'Look at India': Trump Cites 7% Growth to Attack Fed Over High Interest Rates
articles.excerpt: The President held up India's low rates and 7 per cent growth as a model, called the Fed "very political," and claimed US growth could hit 20 per cent — a claim set against official data showing 3.4 per cent.
articles.image_caption: US President Donald Trump speaks at a White House news conference, flanked by Vice President JD Vance and Secretary of State Marco Rubio.
articles.nri_angle: Explains, for Indian Americans weighing mortgages and borrowing costs, that the President's India comparison is pressure on the Fed rather than a rate decision, and sets his growth claims against the official US figures.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Trump Threatens 'Tremendous Tax' on US Firms Building Data Centers Abroad
articles.excerpt: At a White House news conference after his Asia trip, Trump said American companies will be penalized for building AI data centers overseas — but gave no rate, mechanism or date, and said his own officials had not yet been told.
articles.nri_angle: US tech firms' overseas data-center plans — and the Indian American engineers and executives who staff them — face a threatened tax with no published rule yet.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Nikhil Gupta Sentenced to 235 Months in US Prison for Pannun Murder-for-Hire Plot
articles.excerpt: A Manhattan federal judge handed the 55-year-old Indian national 19 years and seven months on Friday, at the bottom of a guidelines range prosecutors had asked to top out at 293 months.
articles.nri_angle: The sentencing closes the criminal case at the centre of the alleged plot against a Sikh separatist on US soil, a case that has strained India-US ties and been closely watched by the Sikh diaspora.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Congress Builds Big Lead Over BJP in Rajasthan Panchayat Polls as Counting Continues
articles.excerpt: With counting still under way across 37 districts, Congress had won 2,990 Panchayat Samiti and 143 Zila Parishad seats in declared results, against 1,795 and 83 for the ruling BJP.
articles.nri_angle: Rajasthan's rural local-body results reshape village-level administration in a state with a large US and Gulf diaspora whose families remain in these panchayats.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Bangladesh PM Rahman Blames India in Veiled Dig as Hasina Supporters' Unrest Spreads
articles.excerpt: Tarique Rahman said the leaders who fled across the border serve "masters" there, as an Awami League lockdown brought arson attacks, arrests and the torching of Muhammad Yunus's ancestral home.
articles.image_caption: Bangladesh Prime Minister Tarique Rahman (left) and former prime minister Sheikh Hasina.
articles.nri_angle: India-Bangladesh tensions over Hasina's exile in India shape regional stability and travel and family ties across the Bengal diaspora.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Ponugoti Twins Build Robotics Nonprofit That Has Reached More Than 1,200 Students
articles.excerpt: Vivaan and Virat Ponugoti started Blast Robotics in Berwyn, Pennsylvania, after one of them was turned away from his school team. Eighteen months on, their Keystone STEM Alliance has mobilized more than $215,000 in support — and runs workshops as far away as Telangana.
articles.image_caption: Twin brothers Virat and Vivaan Ponugoti, co-founders of Blast Robotics, in Berwyn, Pennsylvania.
articles.nri_angle: Two Pennsylvania teenagers of Indian origin turned a school rejection into a STEM nonprofit whose outreach now runs from Berwyn to Telangana.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Indian National Tushar Sharma, 25, Found Dead in Burning Car in Langley
articles.excerpt: British Columbia homicide investigators say the evidence suggests the Surrey resident was targeted. No suspect has been named, and police are appealing for information about his movements before October 29.
articles.image_caption: Tushar Sharma, 25, of Surrey, in a photograph supplied by the Integrated Homicide Investigation Team. IHIT released his name and photograph on November 17, 2026, as it appealed for information in the Langley vehicle-fire homicide.
articles.nri_angle: A 25-year-old Indian national living in Surrey was found dead in a burning car in Langley; IHIT's public appeal for information is aimed squarely at the region's South Asian community.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: World Champion Gukesh Named to TIME100 Next India Weeks Before First Title Defence
articles.excerpt: The 20-year-old appears in the Phenoms category of TIME's first country-specific Next list, with his profile written by Sharda Ugra.
articles.image_caption: World chess champion Gukesh Dommaraju, in the portrait TIME published with its TIME100 Next India list. The 20-year-old appears in the list's Phenoms category, weeks before his first world title defence against Javokhir Sindarov.
articles.nri_angle: A New York magazine's first India list, published for a global audience, puts the Chennai world champion in its Phenoms class days before his title defence.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Indiaspora Names Kiran Ghia an Inspiring Icon for STEM Work in Rural Mississippi
articles.excerpt: As Chief Strategy Advisor at the Global Teaching Project, the Indian American advocate has helped bring free AP STEM classes to more than 4,000 students in over 50 rural Mississippi schools over the past decade.
articles.nri_angle: A child of Indian immigrant professors, Ghia carries her family's education values into rural Mississippi classrooms and is now documenting the Indian teachers serving the Delta.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Hopkins Man Charged With Attempted Murder in Attack on Uber Driver Mohamed Yusuf
articles.excerpt: Samit Apurva Patel, 25, is held on $1 million bail after prosecutors say he strangled Somali American driver Mohamed Yusuf with a seatbelt and ran him over with his own car. Yusuf, 51, is in critical condition, and prosecutors say bias could not be proved beyond a reasonable doubt.
articles.nri_angle: Indian outlets identified the accused as Indian-origin; the case has drawn diaspora attention as prosecutors decline a bias enhancement while the Somali community seeks a federal hate-crime review.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Trump, Xi and Putin Speak at APEC Plenary in Shenzhen Before First Trilateral
articles.excerpt: Xi Jinping opened the Shenzhen plenary with a $20 million cooperation pledge as the three presidents prepared for the first-ever US-China-Russia leaders' meeting, with Iran, nuclear arms and a fragile trade truce in the background.
articles.image_caption: US President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping pose ahead of the APEC family photo in Shenzhen.
articles.nri_angle: India is not an APEC member, but the tariff truce, rare-earth supplies and energy risks negotiated in Shenzhen shape the trade and prices the diaspora lives with; the truce runs to January 10, 2027.

articles.excerpt: A New York federal judge authorised service through three Delhi district courts under the Hague Convention. India rejected the lawsuit's allegations as fabricated and said service requests must go through its Law Ministry.
articles.nri_angle: A US court's procedural ruling in a case brought by a US-based Khalistan activist against India's top security officials, rejected by New Delhi as fabricated.

articles.title: Prince William and Kate Meet Modi in Delhi as Three-Day India Visit Concludes
articles.excerpt: The Prince and Princess of Wales closed their India tour with talks on trade and the new India-UK economic agreement, after a final Mumbai morning split between a Bollywood studio and a maternity hospital.
articles.image_caption: Prince William, Prince of Wales, whose three-day India visit concluded with a meeting with Prime Minister Narendra Modi in Delhi.
articles.nri_angle: The visit closed with a Modi meeting centred on the recently implemented India-UK trade agreement, a deal with direct stakes for the British Indian diaspora.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Mamdani Condemns Racism Against Indian Americans at New York Diwali Event
articles.excerpt: Hosting Diwali at his office, New York's first Indian-American mayor cited attacks on Hindu temples and Sikh Americans and urged a rejection of a “politics of darkness.”
articles.nri_angle: The mayor of America's largest city, himself its first Indian-American mayor, has put temple safety and anti-South Asian hate on the civic agenda the same week lawmakers pressed Washington for a federal probe.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: 13 Lawmakers Seek Federal Probe Into Seattle Diwali Event Disruption
articles.excerpt: All six Indian American House members signed a letter asking the Justice Department to examine whether two men who entered the Seattle Center Armory festival with racial slurs and anti-Hindu signs violated federal civil rights laws, with a briefing requested by December 4.
articles.image_caption: Archival photograph: Seattle Center at dusk, with the Space Needle and the Museum of Pop Culture in the foreground. The campus Armory hosted the Diwali: Lights of India festival on November 7, whose disruption 13 US lawmakers have asked the Justice Department to investigate.
articles.nri_angle: A Diwali festival disruption in Seattle is now a federal civil rights question, with every Indian American member of the House asking the Justice Department to act.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Cyclone Akvan to Hit Andhra Coast Friday With Winds up to 145 Kmph
articles.excerpt: The IMD expects Akvan to strengthen into a very severe cyclonic storm before crossing between Nellore and Visakhapatnam around noon on November 20, with seven Andhra districts on red alert and Odisha evacuating vulnerable villages.
articles.nri_angle: Families across the diaspora with relatives in coastal Andhra Pradesh, Odisha and Tamil Nadu have a two-day window to check in and prepare before Akvan's Friday landfall.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Quad Leaders Announce First Joint Patrol-Aircraft Exercise and Critical Minerals Deals in Manila
articles.excerpt: The Manila summit’s joint statement pairs a 2027 P-8 exercise and a business forum with a warning on economic coercion — while leaving the South China Sea unnamed.
articles.image_caption: From left, Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi, Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi, US President Donald Trump and Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese pose in Manila on November 17, 2026. The four leaders issued a joint statement announcing the first Quad patrol-aircraft exercise and new supply-chain cooperation. Photo: Prime Minister’s Office of Japan.
articles.nri_angle: The Quad’s direction on supply chains, maritime security and AI shapes the Indo-Pacific order that diaspora families’ home countries and trade routes depend on.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: One Indian Seafarer Missing, Two Injured After Hormuz Tanker Attack
articles.excerpt: India condemned the November 16 attack on the LPG tanker MT Tara Gas in the Strait of Hormuz. Twenty-one of the 24 Indians aboard were evacuated to Khasab in Oman, and the search for the missing crew member continues.
articles.image_caption: Satellite view of the Strait of Hormuz and the Musandam Peninsula (NASA MODIS file photo, 2018). The strait is where the tanker MT Tara Gas was attacked.
articles.nri_angle: Indian seafarers crew a large share of Gulf shipping; the embassy in Oman is the coordination point for the Tara Gas crew's families as the search continues.

articles.title: Prince William Opens India Visit in a Handloom Jacket Woven in West Bengal
articles.excerpt: The Prince of Wales played gully cricket and drank kulhad chai with Sachin Tendulkar in Mumbai, wearing a custom KARDO waistcoat, as the three-day Earthshot-centred visit got under way.
articles.nri_angle: A royal visit opening in Mumbai with Indian handloom, gully cricket and the Earthshot Prize speaks directly to the UK-India cultural ties the diaspora lives between.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Trump Calls Modi 'a Very Tough Man' as Quad Leaders Meet in Manila
articles.excerpt: At the first in-person Quad leaders' summit since 2024, Trump praised Modi and Takaichi's toughness while Modi pressed the four nations to set concrete goals on supply chains, technology and security.
articles.nri_angle: The Quad's turn toward funded joint projects in semiconductors, critical minerals and AI infrastructure shapes the strategic environment Indian-American businesses and professionals operate in across the Indo-Pacific.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Chase Software Bug Ripples Across US Banks, Stalling Zelle Payments for Hours
articles.excerpt: A fault in JPMorgan Chase's own systems delayed transactions nationwide on Monday, surfacing as errors at Wells Fargo, Bank of America and other banks whenever a Zelle payment touched Chase. Chase said it was fixed by Monday evening.
articles.nri_angle: Indian Americans banking with Chase, Wells Fargo or Bank of America - and sending money over Zelle - were among those hit by Monday's delays.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Goyal Asks India, Egypt Startups to Co-Build Payments, Health Tech
articles.excerpt: At the Egypt-India Startup Forum in Cairo, the commerce minister proposed cross-border payments built on UPI and InstaPay, plus joint work on water, farms and affordable medical devices.
articles.nri_angle: For Indian founders and investors abroad, the Cairo forum opens a ministerially backed Egypt corridor in payments, agritech and health tech, with an India startup event for Egyptian founders planned for January.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Gates Foundation Pledges Up to $1 Billion for Family Planning Through 2030
articles.excerpt: Announced at the Copenhagen Summit, the commitment puts $694 million into family planning and sits on top of a separate $2.5 billion women's health research pledge from August 2025.
articles.image_caption: The Gates Foundation campus in Seattle, Washington.
articles.nri_angle: Global health funding shapes programmes across South Asia and Africa that diaspora families support and follow; the pledge runs through 2030.

articles.title: US Flight Chaos Rolls Into Sunday: 6,400 Saturday Cancellations, Normal Only Late Sunday
articles.excerpt: The FAA says schedules should largely recover by late Sunday after Friday's ground stop — the longest since 9/11 — as investigators examine two L3Harris routers and airlines waive rebooking fees.
articles.nri_angle: Indian travellers in the US face a second day of mass cancellations; airline waivers allow free rebooking, and Sunday departures remain at risk until the FAA's late-Sunday recovery.

articles.title: Jaishankar Says India-US Trade Deal Is Near the 'Finishing Line'
articles.excerpt: The external affairs minister told the HT Leadership Summit that the bulk of issues, including tariff lines, are resolved — and that most of what remains sits on the American side.
articles.image_caption: Archival photograph: External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar speaks at a podium on November 11, 2026. Jaishankar said on November 14 that India-US trade negotiations are approaching the finishing line, with the bulk of issues resolved.
articles.nri_angle: A sealed deal would reset tariff terms for Indian exporters selling into the US, the largest market for both Indian goods and diaspora-run trade businesses.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Sharif Says Pakistan Can Reach Sixth-Largest Economy Before 2050, Not 2075
articles.excerpt: Addressing a minerals investment forum in Islamabad, Pakistan's prime minister amended a Goldman Sachs projection that places his country sixth in the world by 2075, saying the milestone can arrive more than 25 years earlier.
articles.image_caption: Pakistan Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif. At the Pakistan Minerals Investment Forum in Islamabad on November 13, 2026, Sharif said Pakistan could become the world's sixth-largest economy before 2050.
articles.nri_angle: The Goldman Sachs study Sharif cited ranks India second in the world by 2075, so his bid to pull Pakistan's sixth-place milestone forward to before 2050 is a claim South Asian readers can measure against India's own projected rise.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: US Assures India a Tariff Edge Over Rivals as Trade Deal Nears First Tranche
articles.excerpt: American negotiators have assured India of a comparative tariff advantage over competing economies, Indian officials say, with the first, goods-only tranche targeted for completion by March 2027.
articles.nri_angle: A tariff edge over rival exporters would directly affect Indian businesses supplying the US market and the diaspora professionals and traders tied to those supply chains.
